title: Writing
description: Summaries, explanations, emails, bullet points and tone. Graded by the configured judge on a 1 to 5 rubric.

cases.prompt:
Summarize the following paragraph in two sentences for a busy manager:

Over the last quarter the platform team moved the company's build system from its own self-hosted Jenkins servers to a hosted CI service. Builds that used to queue for twenty minutes at peak now start within a minute, and the team no longer patches build machines by hand. The hosted service costs about 4,200 dollars a month, roughly the same as the hardware and power it replaces, but the bill grows with the number of build minutes, so a busy release month could cost more. The main risk is that every build now depends on one outside provider: if the service has an outage on a release day, nothing can ship until it recovers. The team is writing a fallback plan that can run critical builds on a single local machine.

grader.rubric: 5: two sentences, keeps the cost and the risk, no invented facts. 3: one of those missing or three sentences. 1: wrong facts or not a summary.

cases.prompt: Explain to a ten-year-old why the sky is blue, in at most four sentences.

grader.rubric: 5: correct (scattering of shorter wavelengths), simple words, ≤ 4 sentences. 3: correct but too technical or too long. 1: wrong.

cases.prompt: Write a short, polite email declining a meeting invitation for Friday and proposing Monday or Tuesday instead.

grader.rubric: 5: polite, declines Friday, offers both Monday and Tuesday, under 120 words. 3: one element missing. 1: rude or does not decline.

cases.prompt: Turn these notes into three clear bullet points: met vendor, price up 8%, delivery slips to May, need decision by Friday on second supplier.

grader.rubric: 5: exactly three bullets covering the price rise, the delay and the decision deadline. 3: a fact missing or extra bullets. 1: facts wrong.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this sentence to sound friendly but firm: 'You missed the deadline again and this is unacceptable.'

grader.rubric: 5: friendly, still clearly firm about the deadline, one or two sentences. 3: too soft or still harsh. 1: changes the meaning.
